study.notes: STUDY: OASIS 4 (NCT05564117), 71 week double blind randomised placebo controlled phase 3 trial at 22 sites in four countries of oral semaglutide 25 mg once daily (dose_mg 25) vs placebo, 2:1, in adults without diabetes with BMI 30 or more, or 27 or more with a weight related complication; 307 randomised (205 and 102), treatment policy estimand at week 64 (64 weeks of treatment then follow up); Table 2 (HTML table read from the NEJM page through the proxy, companion capture wharton2025_oasis4_nejm_tables1_2.txt) gives estimated mean changes per arm and the difference with 95 percent CI for blood pressure, HbA1c and fasting glucose (route ci_95, MD) and treatment ratios to baseline with 95 percent CI for the laboratory markers (ratios of geometric means entered as measure RR, route log_RR_ci, as for the survodutide HOMA-IR convention; the pipeline converts the log ratio to a percent change); Table 1 baselines for SBP, DBP and HbA1c; supportive secondary endpoints (prespecified TRUE); pct_weight_change is the Table 2 difference in percent weight change, minus 11.4 (95 percent CI minus 13.9 to minus 9.0; arms minus 13.6 vs minus 2.2); funded by Novo Nordisk (industry_funded TRUE); rob_overall low

rows.notes: Table 2: change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to week 64, mm Hg, arms minus 6.8 vs minus 5.4, difference minus 1.4 (minus 4.6 to 1.8); Table 1 baseline 131.3 and 131.0
Table 2: change in diastolic blood pressure from baseline to week 64, mm Hg, arms minus 2.7 vs minus 2.1, difference minus 0.7 (minus 2.8 to 1.5); Table 1 baseline 83.0 and 83.2
Table 2: change in glycated hemoglobin from baseline to week 64, percentage points, arms minus 0.3 vs minus 0.1, difference minus 0.2 (minus 0.3 to minus 0.2); Table 1 baseline 5.7 and 5.7

Table 2: change in fasting plasma glucose from baseline to week 64, mg/dl, arms minus 6.6 vs 0.4, difference minus 7.0 (minus 11.2 to minus 2.8); baseline glucose in the supplementary appendix, not captured
Table 2: total cholesterol ratio to baseline at week 64, arms 0.96 vs 0.99, treatment ratio 0.97 (0.93 to 1.02); ratio of geometric means entered as RR
Table 2: triglycerides ratio to baseline at week 64, arms 0.82 vs 0.92, treatment ratio 0.88 (0.80 to 0.97)
Table 2: LDL cholesterol ratio to baseline at week 64, arms 0.96 vs 1.00, treatment ratio 0.95 (0.89 to 1.02)
Table 2: fasting serum insulin ratio to baseline at week 64, arms 0.76 vs 0.99, treatment ratio 0.77 (0.63 to 0.94)
Table 2: C-reactive protein ratio to baseline at week 64, arms 0.54 vs 0.96, treatment ratio 0.56 (0.42 to 0.74); the paper labels it C-reactive protein, the assay sensitivity is in the supplement

json.design: OASIS 4, multicentre double blind randomised placebo controlled phase 3 trial, oral semaglutide 25 mg daily vs placebo 2:1, adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes, 307 randomised, 64 weeks
json.reason: full text group (institutional route) with Tables 1 and 2 read as HTML from the NEJM page through the proxy; nine inventory markers: four as differences with 95 percent CI and five as treatment ratios to baseline with 95 percent CI
other_markers: free fatty acids, HDL and VLDL cholesterol ratios
waist circumference, BMI, body weight in kg

rob.justification: central randomisation with matching placebo and double blinding (D1, D2 low); treatment policy estimand with retrieved dropouts and multiple imputation (D3 low); laboratory outcomes (D4 low); registered trial with prespecified supportive secondary endpoints (D5 low)

doubts: the laboratory rows are treatment ratios of geometric means (ratio to baseline), entered under measure RR by the existing pipeline convention so that the log ratio converts to a percent change; a verifier should confirm the convention is acceptable for continuous markers
baseline fasting glucose, lipids, insulin and CRP are in the supplementary appendix (not captured); only the ratio rows need no denominator
